clue.text: Caught a fish near eastern waterfall

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
the scad is a horse mackerel, a sea fish

explanation.surface: An angler lands a catch beside a waterfall to the east.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade is a small waterfall, or a series of them tumbling down rocks.

clue.text: A ship, say, with first-rate weapon

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
say means for example, abbreviated eg
A1 is first-rate, written as AI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A vessel, for instance, comes equipped with a top-quality weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 meaning first-rate is written AI, the digit 1 standing as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: An assegai is a slender iron-tipped spear used in southern Africa.

clue.text: Capital atmosphere in a small business house

indicators.note: in says the word for atmosphere sits inside the abbreviation for a company

parts.note: Co is the short form of company, a business house
the atmosphere is the air around us

explanation.surface: The mood inside a little firm's office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small' means abbreviated: a business house is a company, shortened to CO, with AIR inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cairo is the capital city of Egypt.

clue.text: Locked up as a final course

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: having locks of hair means having tresses

explanation.surface: Imprisoned as a last resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locked' means not imprisoned but having locks of hair; 'up' turns TRESSED round in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Dessert is the sweet course served at the end of a meal.

clue.text: Make a mark as a non-runner

definitions.meaning: to score a line on a surface
a horse that is ... is withdrawn from its race

explanation.definitionFit: Scratching marks a surface, and a scratched horse is struck off the race card.

clue.text: Grubby residence

parts.note: read not as a dirty home but as the home of a grub, an insect larva

explanation.definitionFit: A silk casing spun by a larva to shelter in while it becomes a pupa.

clue.text: A rich man's form of lawlessness

indicators.note: form of says the letters are shaped into a new word

explanation.surface: Wealthy people have their own brand of disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges A RICH MANS, the S of the possessive counting here.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchism is the doctrine of rejecting government, the absence of law.

clue.text: Fair weather saint?

definitions.meaning: describes weather that is mild and pleasant

explanation.definitionFit: The word means mild in weather and is the name of the saint and pope.

clue.text: A top-liner in the beauty parlour

definitions.text: A top-liner in the beauty parlour

parts.words: A top-liner in the beauty parlour
parts.note: a 'top-liner' read not as a star performer but as something that draws lines above the eyes

explanation.definitionFit: This cosmetic is used to darken and shape the brows above the eyes.

clue.text: Wine from west part of east Italy?

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a wine from the western side of eastern Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The wine Asti in fact comes from Piedmont in north-west Italy, hence 'from west'; the question mark marks the hidden-word joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling white wine made in Piedmont, north-western Italy.

clue.text: Big build-up in New York, for example

definitions.text: Big build-up in New York, for example

parts.words: Big build-up in New York, for example
parts.note: a 'build-up' read literally is a construction rising very high, of the kind Manhattan is famous for

explanation.definitionFit: Very tall buildings, famously those of New York, are the towers that seem to graze the heavens.

clue.text: Soldier returns to scene of mutiny and neglect

indicators.note: returns means the soldier's letters are read backwards

parts.note: GI is an American private soldier
the Nore, a Thames estuary anchorage, saw a famous naval mutiny in 1797

explanation.surface: A soldier goes back to where a mutiny broke out and finds neglect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns GI into IG. THE NORE is a sandbank anchorage at the mouth of the Thames, where the Royal Navy mutinied in 1797.
explanation.definitionFit: To neglect something is to pay it no attention, to disregard it.

clue.text: Breaks the surface off Abersoch

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong or out of order, so the place name is rearranged

explanation.surface: Something surfaces in the sea off the Welsh resort of Abersoch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like a preposition placing the action near Abersoch, a sailing village in north Wales, but it signals an anagram of ABERSOCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A whale or submarine that broaches rises and breaks through the surface of the water.

clue.text: Point of order?

parts.note: read not as a meeting procedure but as a compass point, and as a word meaning an instruction or order

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a compass bearing one points along and an instruction given to someone.

clue.text: Package turned up, given address with added detail

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue says the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a bale is a bound package of goods
to orate is to address an audience

explanation.surface: A parcel arrived, was addressed, and its details filled in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses BALE to ELAB in this down entry; 'given' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elaborate is detailed and intricate, worked out with care.

clue.text: New arrival at the docks, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word for a ship's mooring is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a ship at the docks is moored at its berth

explanation.surface: A ship pulls into the docks, apparently, as a new arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: A birth brings a baby into the world, a newcomer in the family.

clue.text: Point-to-point express

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass
a peak is a pointed summit

explanation.surface: A point-to-point horse race is run at express speed.
explanation.walkthrough: A point-to-point is a British amateur steeplechase; 'express' looks like 'fast' but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To express a thought is to put it into words, to say it.

clue.text: An explorer needing one in support

indicators.note: in says one word sits inside the word for support

parts.note: a pier is a pillar supporting a bridge or arch
taken as written

explanation.surface: An explorer needs someone to back them up.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer is one of the first to explore or settle a new region.

clue.text: Possibly meant to secure some accommodation

indicators.note: to secure means the rearranged word holds another piece fast inside it
possibly says the letters of the next word are only one possible arrangement

parts.note: some, as in a portion, is part

explanation.surface: Someone might have intended to book a place to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges the clue's 'meant' as AMENT; 'some' looks like a quantifier but is the noun for a portion, held inside after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: An apartment is a set of rooms to live in, a form of accommodation.

clue.text: Continued to give the total in a rush

indicators.note: in says the word for totting up goes inside the plant

parts.note: a rush is a waterside plant, like a reed
to sum is to add up and give the total

explanation.surface: Someone carried on, hurriedly giving a total.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a rush' looks like haste but is the marsh plant; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To have resumed is to have carried on again after a pause.

clue.text: A celebrity, despite lack of talent

parts.note: lacking something, one is not possessed of it
talented means able, skilled

explanation.surface: A famous person who has no gift at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'despite' is a link: lack of talent means NOT ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A notable is a person of note, someone famous or eminent.

clue.text: Clothing articles dropped by Boadicea

indicators.note: dropped by says these letters are taken out of the queen's name

parts.note: A is the indefinite article, so articles give two As

explanation.surface: The warrior queen sheds some of her garments.
explanation.walkthrough: BOADICEA, queen of the Iceni who fought the Romans, loses both of her As.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodice is the close-fitting upper part of a woman's dress, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Make a great effort to leave the country

definitions.meaning: the idiom means to do something lavishly or with great energy
read literally, a rural dweller heading into the big town

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means acting with great energy, and literally it is a trip from the countryside into town.

clue.text: Conceited midshipman

definitions.meaning: in old naval slang, a junior officer cadet was called by this name

explanation.definitionFit: The word means snooty or supercilious, and was naval slang for a midshipman.

clue.text: Fantastic to be out and about

parts.note: taken as written
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: It is great to be out and about.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré, from French, means bizarre or unconventional, far beyond the usual.

clue.text: Contrary to accepted beliefs, it can be time-saving

indicators.note: it can be says the following letters can be rearranged into the answer

explanation.surface: A contrarian view that it might save time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it can be' signals that TIME-SAVING (ten letters, hyphen ignored) rearranges into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Negativism is a habit of denial and opposition to what others accept or suggest.

clue.text: Underground TV

definitions.meaning: the London Underground railway is nicknamed this

explanation.definitionFit: It is London's nickname for the Underground and slang for the television set.

clue.text: Given command, other ranks run into action

parts.note: OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, i.e. not officers

indicators.note: into says the abbreviation for run goes inside the word for action

parts.note: a deed is an act or action
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Soldiers given an order run into action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts R inside DEED to give DERED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ordered has been commanded, as an officer gives an instruction.

clue.text: Attached to a refined redhead

indicators.note: refined means processed or reworked, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has grown fond of a sophisticated red-haired person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refined' looks like praise for the redhead, but it rearranges REDHEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: To have adhered to something is to have stuck or become fixed to it.
